steps.label: Volatility clustering: big moves follow big moves
This asymmetry is why volatility is its own field
First step: measure it correctly from data

code:
import numpy as np

returns = prices.pct_change().dropna()
hist_vol_20d = returns.rolling(window=20).std()

# annualize assuming ~252 trading days/year
annualized_vol = hist_vol_20d * np.sqrt(252)
caption: Equally weights every return in the trailing window; simple, but can jump when old data drops out.

code:
# intraday_returns: 5-minute log returns, indexed by timestamp
daily_rv = (
    intraday_returns.pow(2)
    .groupby(intraday_returns.index.date)
    .sum()
    .pow(0.5)
)
caption: RV_t = sqrt(sum of squared intraday returns) — a more efficient estimator than one daily close-to-close return.
